articleTitle: A New Autonomous Control Level in the Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The Hungarian power system is over penetrated by PhotoVoltaic generation. The daily trade direction tend to change from import to export depending on the weather. Meanwhile the import and export should be decreased. A new autonomous control level is recommended for involving millions of the small household through Household Control Box. Based on latest real data the effect of three different control strategies are shown. By the rescheduling of the local usage and generation we reduced the load of the transmission system, the import/export. Meanwhile the share of the domestic use of PV production has increased. The autonomous control level help to cope with control of the more and more complex power system.

articleTitle: Concept and Considerations for the Development of an Information Database for Efficient International Freight Transport
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: International freight transport is a growing market and a crucial component of the global economy, enabling the seamless flow of goods across regions and supporting global trade. However, the industry faces significant challenges, particularly in road transport orchestration, due to the increasing complexity of operations and the demand for real-time decision-making. This study sketched the algorithmic and programming framework to address these challenges by presenting an optimized database architecture designed to improve decision support systems for freight transport. The proposed system architecture may leverage the flexibility and scalability of NoSQL databases to manage large, semi-structured datasets in the future, while REST APIs enable seamless integration and real-time data manipulation. To enhance usability and transparency, the system incorporates advanced data visualization tools, allowing stakeholders to derive actionable insights and improve operational efficiency. By focusing on areas such as real-time tracking, sustainability, and process optimization, this work not only addresses current operational needs but also provides a robust foundation for future developments, including advanced analytics and mobile application integration. This contribution supports the logistics industry's shift toward more adaptive, efficient, and sustainable transport solutions.

articleTitle: The Importance of Collaboration Skills in Agile Workplaces
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Agile methodologies are gaining ground not only in the IT sector but also in other industries. The importance of collaboration skills in the modern workplace has increased exponentially with the rise of agile working.. At the heart of the agile approach are flexibility, adaptability and teamwork, all of which are closely linked to effective collaboration. Rather than traditional hierarchical structures, agile organisations are built around smaller, autonomous teams where shared goals and responsibilities prevail. This environment requires employees to be able to communicate effectively, share information and work together to achieve a common goal. Successful collaboration not only enables projects to be completed faster and more efficiently, but also fosters innovation and creativity, which is a key factor for competitive advantage in the 21st century. In an agile workplace, team members need to be able to adapt quickly to changing circumstances, receive and give feedback constructively and actively participate in joint problem-solving. In our research, we investigate the collaboration skills that are perceived as most important by employees in companies using agile methodologies, based on the results of a primary survey. The study was based on a survey of 274 respondents, and we were interested in how important they consider the different skills and competences required for collaboration to be. The aim of our survey is to identify the most important areas for improvement, pointing organisations in the right direction both in building more effective organisations and in developing their staff.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Cybersecurity: A Review on Network Threat Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The increasing complexity of network systems and the rise of IoT (Internet of Things) devices have significantly increased the risk of cybersecurity threats, especially in the areas of ransomware, DDoS, malware attacks, and data security threats. This study examines the application of deep learning technologies in detecting and managing network threats. Deep learning models such as autoencoder, CNN, RNN, and GAN can detect anomalies and identify attacks with outstanding accuracy. The results of the study highlight that deep learning technologies are not only suitable for addressing current threats, but also have significant potential in shaping future cybersecurity strategies.

articleTitle: Design of Experiments for Learning Dynamic Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Optimal experimental designs were discussed first in the statistical literatures as allocation problem of points in classical regression problems. This was soon followed by designing optimal input or excitation signals under special constraints to get a kind of best estimation of parametrized models from measured data. These procedures were very useful to get the minimal number of experiments to achieve a certain quality of the estimated parameters or frequency response

articleTitle: The Financial Awareness of Hungarian Enterprises in Financial Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The study examines the financial awareness of Hungarian enterprises in terms of the conditions of financial decision making. Financial literacy plays a key role in the life of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), influencing their operations and success in a number of areas. Enterprises with a higher level of financial literacy are more likely to avoid adverse financial decisions and improve the positive outcomes of the decisions they make, which contributes to their long-term competitiveness. Financially literate SMEs manage risks more effectively and are better prepared to face the challenges of growth. Financial awareness helps businesses to access finance more efficiently, maintain cash-flow balance and reduce indebtedness, which is key to survival and growth. It also helps to make informed financial decisions and develop a company-specific financial strategy, improving the efficiency of overall operations. At the macroeconomic level, improving the financial awareness of SMEs contributes to the stability, growth and competitiveness of the country's economy. The research presented in this study was based on a questionnaire survey of 655 enterprises, which sought to find out who and how financial decisions are made in the Hungarian business sector. The results show that the size and type of enterprises have a significant impact on decision-making processes, providing direction and examples for the future success of the actors in the entrepreneurial sector.

articleTitle: Conscious Food Shopping, Getting Information About Food from a Gender Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The study of food consumption behaviour is crucial in modern societies where sustainability, health consciousness and the complexity of global supply chains are increasingly under scrutiny. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the factors influencing food consumption decisions, including cultural, economic, social and psychological aspects. Our analysis pays particular attention to the demand for sustainable food and the rise of ethical consumer behaviour. The research uses a quantitative approach to investigate food consumers' preferences and motivations, while also exploring the relationship between price sensitivity and purchasing behaviour. The results show that changes in consumer behaviour are closely linked to growing awareness of social and environmental issues.

articleTitle: Quantum Machine Learning in Crop Disease Monitoring: Opportunities and Challenges to Practical Implementation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Agriculture is increasingly threatened by diverse global security challenges, including climate change, biodiversity loss, and health security risks, underscoring the need for sustainable practices to ensure food security for future generations. Advanced technologies such as quantum machine learning (QML) offer transformative potential in addressing these challenges by enhancing crop disease monitoring systems. This paper explores the implementation of QML in agriculture, with a particular focus on its application to crop disease detection and prevention. Leveraging image processing, sensory data analysis, and spectral imaging, QML algorithms demonstrate superior accuracy and efficiency in early disease recognition, surpassing traditional methods. A case study of Hungary's crop disease monitoring system illustrates the practical benefits of integrating QML with technologies such as remote sensing and IoT. By enabling real-time monitoring and predictive analytics, QML not only aids in mitigating crop losses but also contributes to sustainable agricultural practices and global food security. Despite current limitations in quantum hardware, advancements in QML present promising opportunities for revolutionizing agricultural systems and ensuring resilience against evolving threats.

articleTitle: Reachability Distance-Based Vector Median Filter: A Novel Method for Image Denoising
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: This paper proposes a generalization of the Vector Median Filter (VMF) for suppressing impulsive noise in color images. The new filtering approach is based on the reachability distance, which enables the incorporation of pixels similarities within their local neighborhoods. The structure of the proposed technique is inspired by the Sharpening VMF (SVMF), which effectively suppresses impulsive noise while enhancing image edges. The proposed method further improves robustness against noise corruption while maintaining edge-sharpening capabilities. Experimental results demonstrate that the new filter significantly outperforms both the VMF and SVMF in terms of objective quality metrics. Visual assessments confirm the efficient removal of noisy pixel clusters without introducing color artifacts. The design is computationally efficient, making it suitable for preprocessing heavily corrupted color images. Additionally, it provides a flexible framework for developing filter families utilizing reduced ordering concepts.

articleTitle: Gender Analysis of Corporate Social Responsibility and its Impact on Consumption
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Social responsibility and conscious consumption have become one of the most important social, economic and environmental challenges of our time. The aim of this article is to explore the relationship between these two concepts, to show how corporate social responsibility (CSR) influences consumers' purchasing decisions and how conscious consumer behaviour is evolving. The analysis will examine the effectiveness of CSR strategies, with a particular focus on the extent to which they can encourage sustainable consumption patterns. The study is based on quantitative research to explore consumer attitudes and expectations towards sustainable products and services. The results show that a commitment to social responsibility can increase brand loyalty and positively influence the perception of companies, but we also highlight barriers to conscious consumer behaviour, such as lack of information or price sensitivity. The paper concludes that conscious consumption and social responsibility are mutually reinforcing factors that need to be integrated for a sustainable future.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fractional Order PI-PD Controllers Applied on a DC Modular Servo System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Fractional calculus extends traditional calculus and provides a comprehensive framework for modelling and control via fractional-order transfer functions (FOTFs). Fractional-order (FO) controllers, including FO-PI and FO-PD, enhance flexibility and performance through the inclusion of an additional tuning parameter, surpassing classical controllers. Despite these advantages, the robustness of FO controllers remains uncertain under varying operating conditions, particularly in nonlinear systems. Adaptive control methods, including Model-Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC), effectively mitigate this limitation by facilitating real-time adjustments to variations in process parameters. This study presents a new control strategy that integrates MRAC with FO control techniques to improve the adaptability and robustness of DC servo motor systems. The DC servo motor, represented as a first-order system, provides the environment for experimental validation. This paper presents the mathematical relations used for tuning the FO-PI and the adaptive FO-PI controllers. The results indicate that this hybrid approach outperforms the classical approach. This research presents the integration of FO and adaptive control for industrial applications.

articleTitle: Intelligent Robotic Assistance in Precision Surgery: Vision, Automation, and Human-Robot Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Surgical robotics has revolutionized modern medicine, enhancing precision, safety, and efficiency in complex procedures. However, many surgical fields, including ophthalmology, continue to rely heavily on manual techniques, demanding exceptional dexterity, coordination, and sustained focus from surgeons. The next frontier in robotic surgery lies in intelligent systems that integrate real-time perception, automation, and human-robot collaboration to enhance surgical outcomes while reducing surgeon workload. This talk presents an overview of our research on intelligent robotic assistance for precision surgery, with a focus on vision-based robotic systems for ophthalmic and microsurgical procedures. One of our key innovations is an intelligent vision-based robotic-assisted system for vitreoretinal surgery, which enhances intraoperative safety through real-time scene understanding, automates surgical lighting to improve visualization, and records surgical actions for skill assessment and training. Beyond ophthalmology, our work extends to developing AI-driven robotic systems for other surgical applications, enabling autonomous assistance in delicate operations where precision and real-time decision-making are critical. By integrating computer vision, machine learning, and robotic automation, our research aims to push the boundaries of robotic surgery, making procedures safer, more efficient, and accessible to a broader range of surgeons. This talk will explore the challenges and breakthroughs in intelligent surgical robotics, the role of AI in enhancing human dexterity, and the future of robotic-assisted surgery in various medical domains.

articleTitle: Security Review of a Client-side Code Execution with HTML Smuggling Attack
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The use of JavaScript and HTML5 is a technique that is widely employed in offensive security to smuggle malicious files past content filters. It is thus not a new approach. However, by considering novel techniques for antivirus evasion, this becomes a topic of high interest. We have also learned that many defenders (blue teams) are technically unaware of this mechanism and its implications. This combination has been incorporated into well-known frameworks that are offensive-related, such as SharpShooter and Demiguise, for example. The first tool is for retrieval and execution of arbitrary CSharp source code. It can also be used for creating payloads in various formats, including HTA, JS, VBS, and WSF. The second tool is aimed at generating. Html files that contain an encrypted HTA file. From our previous work, we have performed our research on the impact of Client-Side Code Execution with Microsoft Office” [1]. We have demonstrated several ways to obtain a reverse shell after a successful execution of a phishing attack. We also tested our malicious executable manually by downloading it and running it on a victim's machine (lab machine) before we performed the phishing activity. This worked well as an example, since nowadays, attackers often use very discreet delivery methods. Another example is by embedding a webpage in an email in a link format. When the victim opens the email and visits the link, JavaScript code will sneak the HTML code, hence HTML Smuggling, to automatically save the dropper file. This method leverages the HTML5 download attribute for anchor tags which tells the web browser to automatically download a file when a user clicks the defined hyperlink. This paper will focus primarily on the creation of the executable file and appliance of the parameters aforementioned using our attacker machine (Kali) and an Apache server.

articleTitle: Integrated Representation of Research by Intelligent Content
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: This paper introduces intelligent content driven autonomous reactive and in any stage executable experimental model of research for high automation related topics. Experimental models accommodate content items during fundamental or problem-solving purposed research in applied informatics together with the related applied mathematics, systemics and medical engineering. Experimental models are developed in research-dedicated collaborative spaces which are placed in professional cloud and organize content items. Research processes, representations, simulations, and results are defined by participants with appropriate roles and credentials and generated by APPs in an engineering modeling platform (EMP). In this paper, objectives of the research in research modeling are introduced in wide context, integrated characteristics and intelligent knowledge driven content of the experimental model are introduced, application of research model in medical engineering is discussed, and implementation of the proposed modeling on EMP is concluded.

articleTitle: Robotic Implementation of Brain-Inspired Multi-Sensory Integration and Decision Making
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Robot autonomy becomes increasingly prolific with the development of advanced artificially intelligent technologies. Embodied robotics is related to real-time interaction of the robot platforms with the environment. An important aspect of embod-ied robotics is the use of multi-sensory information fusion for robust autonomous decisions and actions. Biologically-inspired approaches to multi-sensory integration (Gestalt formation) gained popularity in embodied robotics due to their flexibility and robustness in noisy and unpredictable practical scenarios. In this work, we discuss dynamic behaviors in multi-robot interaction which emerge as a result of implementing cognitively-motivated multi-sensory integration and action selection. A testbed using mobile quadruped Spot robots is proposed, to evaluate hypotheses on the formation of sequential communication patterns in robot-robot collaboration.

articleTitle: Development of Population Norms with the Robot Anxiety Scale Measurement Tool for Hungary
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The development of social and assistive robots raise the question of societal readiness level to accept and use these advanced technologies. The Robot Anxiety Scale (RAS) is one of the most frequently applied measurement tools to assess robot-related anxiety, however reference scores from the general population with RAS are still lacking. The aim of our study was to establish population norms with the RAS for Hungary. An online cross-sectional survey was performed among the adult general population of Hungary (N=1000; mean age 48.9, SD=10.0; female: 53.3%). Participants completed the validated Hungarian version of the RAS. The average RAS subscale scores were: Communication Capability 10.1 (SD=3.9), Behavioral Characteristics 13.7 (SD=5.3) and Discourse with Robots 13.5 (SD=5.4). Female and less educated respondents reported significantly higher anxiety scores on all the three RAS subscales, but no significant difference was found by age. Results of this first RAS population norms study can be used as reference points for further clinical studies and as basic inputs for the implementation and management of social, assistive and healthcare robots in cyber-medical systems. Prospective multi-country studies among the elderly and offline samples are encouraged to complement the results.

articleTitle: Gamified AI-Driven Video Monitoring for Enhanced Rehabilitation in Performance Sports
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The paper addresses a critical intersection of rehabilitation, performance optimization, and athlete engagement through an AI-supported technological pipeline. By leveraging gamification for engagement and AI pipelines for precision, it represents a paradigm shift in how injuries are managed in performance sports, ultimately leading to healthier athletes, more efficient recovery processes, and improved long-term outcomes in competitive environments. Designing a complex AI -supported gamification system in sport rehabilitation involves creating a comprehensive framework that incorporates user engagement, behavior modification, and continuous learning through AI-driven insights. The proposed solution accurately monitors and analyzes athletic performance, leading to individualized rehabilitation and strategy-hardening procedures.

articleTitle: Evaluating Dysgraphia Level Using Handwriting Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: This study investigates the use of machine learning for assessing dysgraphia severity through handwriting analysis. Handwriting data were collected from eight distinct tasks per-formed by children diagnosed with dysgraphia and matched controls, recorded using a Wacom tablet. Each sample was manually graded by trained professionals to establish severity levels. Features related to spatiotemporal dynamics, kinematics, and pressure were extracted and used to train an XGBoost classifier, with cross-validation ensuring robust evaluation. The results showed task-specific performance differences, with the highest accuracy of 61.89% for sentence-writing and 60.15% for single-letter writing. Tasks involving longer words or pseudowords showed lower performance due to increased motor and cognitive demands. Low inter-rater agreement among human evaluators highlighted the Subjectivity of manual grading, underscoring the potential of automated, objective assessment methods. These findings support the use of machine learning in dysgraphia evaluation while emphasizing the need for improved task designs and feature optimization for broader clinical and educational applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Slovak Natural Language Processing: Fine-Tuning Sentence BERT Models with Translated MS MARCO V2 Data Using MADLAD-400
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: This study explores the enhancement of Slovak Natural Language Processing (NLP) by fine-tuning Sentence BERT models using the translated MS MARCO V2 dataset, facilitated by the MADLAD-400 language model. We translated the MS MARCO V2 dataset into Slovak and utilized this translation to train Sentence BERT models, aiming to improve the quality of vector representations for Slovak sentences. Employing a triplet network approach, we derived meaningful sentence vector representations, enabling effective comparison through cosine similarity. The research yields a newly translated database and evaluates the performance of fine-tuned Slovak vector representation models, thereby advancing Slovak search capabilities.

articleTitle: Design of a Modular Enclosed Chamber for use in 3D Printing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The aim of the paper was to design an enclosed chamber that would provide a stable and controlled environment for the 3D printing process. The practical part involved the design of the enclosed chamber using the PTC Creo Parametric software, which allowed for accurate modelling and optimisation of the components. Furthermore, the components were fabricated using additive manufacturing, specifically FDM printing, and assembled into a functional assembly. This design addressed the need to minimize the impact of external influences, such as temperature and humidity, which can negatively affect 3D printing results. The final design meets all specified functional requirements. The modular design provides flexibility and adaptability for a variety of printer sizes, making it suitable for a wide range of applications. It has a positive impact on the working environment around the 3D printer, as the process can emit particles that affect air quality. The enclosure helps to reduce these emissions and increases safety during the work. Testing has confirmed that the chamber creates a stable environment, leading to improved print quality.

articleTitle: Multivariable Control in General Anesthesia: A Comparative Study of Model Predictive and Fractional-Order Strategies for Effect-Site Concentration and Hemodynamic Regulation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Managing anesthesia and hemodynamic regulation during surgical procedures poses significant challenges due to patient-specific variability and the complex interactions of administered drugs. While advanced monitoring systems and Target-Controlled Infusion (TCI) devices enhance precision in drug delivery, their reliance on manual adjustments limits real-time adaptability. This study investigates two advanced control strategies–centralized Model Predictive Control (MPC) and decentralized fractional-order control–within a multivariable framework designed to regulate hypnosis, analgesia, and hemodynamic stabilization. Virtual patient simulations were used to evaluate these approaches under diverse anesthetic and, notably, hemodynamic conditions. The findings reveal that MPC delivers superior precision in maintaining the Bispectral Index (BIS) but tends to apply more aggressive adjustments to hemodynamic variables. In contrast, fractional-order control ensures smoother responses, though its ability to handle disturbances is less robust in certain scenarios. This study highlights the trade-offs between these strategies and advocates for further exploration of hybrid solutions to enhance patient safety and surgical outcomes.

articleTitle: Advanced Examination Systems: Applying Fuzzy Logic and Machine Learning Methods in Education
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: In our paper, we present an innovative educational assessment system that attempts to overcome the limitations of traditional educational evaluation methods by applying machine learning, artificial intelligence, fuzzy logic, and advanced mathematical techniques. This system can provide a more objective and personalized assessment of students’ knowledge. Current examination systems in educational institutions are outdated and do not meet modern societal and technological requirements. A central element of the system is the application of fuzzy logic, which allows for handling uncertainties in knowledge assessment. Using the FP-growth algorithm and the fuzzy analytical hierarchy process (AHP) aids in optimizing the evaluation process and enables a more profound analysis of students’ performance. During the system's development, we aim to adaptively manage the difficulty level of questions, taking into account students’ prior performance and individual capabilities. The study highlights the security risks and efficiency issues of current “manual” question compilation methods. The new system aims to minimize these risks while improving the quality of education and reducing the workload of educators.

articleTitle: Sorting Objects Using the Vision System of the Robot
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Currently, robots and robotics as a field of science have expanded to be used in almost all industrial areas as well as in everyday life. The current direction of the automation of industrial production is oriented towards the introduction of machines and devices enabling the automatic execution and management of work previously performed by a conventional machine and worker. These automatically controlled devices relieve workers not only from monotonous physical work, but also mental activity, and at the same time improve productivity, quality of processes and products. The article describes the design of a robotic application for automatic sorting of components using a vision camera system. It points to the creation of the control program and the definition of the necessary settings in the software interface necessary for the correct operation of the used robotic arm. The result of the design is a functional robotic workplace developed for the automated sorting of post tensioning wedges as a detected object according to their hole diameter, pointing out the possibility of using machine vision in robotics.

articleTitle: Edge-Cloud Infrastructure for Mushroom Growth Monitoring and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents the development and implementation of an edge-cloud infrastructure for monitoring and analyzing white and brown button mushroom growth. The system includes edge devices with sensors and cameras for onsite data collection and a cloud platform for data storage and processing. The collected data is processed using a Mask R-CNN model trained on synthetic data to identify and analyze individual mushrooms. Over two years of monitoring, it has demonstrated reliability in capturing and processing data in challenging agricultural environments. These results highlight the potential of integrating advanced machine learning with edge-cloud systems to enhance precision agriculture and resource management.

articleTitle: Service Life Modeling of Pavement with Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Random Forest (RF) is an ensemble learning which creates multiple decision trees and combines their outputs for creating models with less over-fitting. In this study, we apply RF to model the remaining service life (RSL) of rural pavements, a critical factor for developing optimal maintenance strategies and ensuring long-lasting infrastructure. We utilize key variables such as asphalt concrete thickness, base thickness, and surface temperature, along with data from Falling Weight Deflectometer (FWD) measurements. RF demonstrated performance in predicting RSL with consistent accuracy across a variety of conditions. The ensemble nature of RF allows it to effectively manage complex interactions among variables and handle the inherent variability in pavement performance data which makes it well-suited for rural road networks, where environmental and material differences are significant. While some sensitivity to parameter adjustments was noted, the robustness and reliability of RF highlights its potential to be a transformative tool in rural pavement management.

articleTitle: Integration of NGS Genomic Metadata Analysis with Open-Source Genomic Databases for Single Cell Tissue Samples
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we present the development and use of an automated platform that integrates the evaluation of genomic metadata from single-cells in colorectal tissues with the open source KEGG genomic database via API using the Biopython package. The system collects and fuses the information into its own PostgreSQL database, from which the results of the analysis are transferred to a graphical user interface using the NpgSql extension. Thus, the implemented application allows the identification of molecular pathways and gene-specific drug targets associated with the mutated genes per cell, providing the combined visualization of tumor diagnostics and gene therapy opportunities. Using the application, 9 predefined gene panels, containing 2800 genes, were analyzed based on which the molecular pathway and drug target coverage of the genes, as well as the correlation between the pathways and drug target values were evaluated.

articleTitle: Wearables and Activity Trackers Market Among University Students: A Narrative Review
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Wearable technologies, such as activity trackers, smartwatches, smart rings, and other sensor-equipped innovative devices worn on the body, have become increasingly popular in the past years. This paper aims to provide a narrative review of scientific evidence and market insights on wearable technologies, with a special focus on their use among university students and social relevance within the environmental, social and governance (ESG) framework. Available literature highlights the advantages of wearables in their ability to continuously monitor and collect real-world health data, and their potential to support personalized lifestyle changes and precision medicine. Scientific evidence regarding their data quality, validity, and reliability are often incomplete or unconvincing. Despite the uncertainties on their measurement accuracy, the global market for wearables is rapidly expanding, driven by technological innovation and increasing health awareness. University students are typically early adopters of innovative high-tech wearables. The usability of wearables in education (e.g., to improve the effectiveness of education or to monitor students' wellbeing) is an intense research area. Studies on the preparedness of universities to support students in using wearables responsibly, recommendations on how to integrate wearables into educational programs and dialogues on ethical implications are lagging behind. Further research and elaboration of effective measures to ensure data privacy and cybersecurity in the university context are needed.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Segmentation from Multi-Spectral MRI Records: Classical Machine Learning or Convolutional Neural Networks?
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Brain tumor segmentation, which involves identifying distinct components like the enhancing core and edema, is a crucial task for ensuring accurate diagnoses and optimizing radiotherapy planning or post-intervention monitoring. However, this process is highly challenging due to the variability in lesion appearances, the potential for noise interference, and differences in MRI scanner sensitivity. This paper represents a comparative study in which XGBoost, the ultimate classical machine learning based method competes with U-net, a well established convolutional network architecture, both being assisted with the adequate preprocessing so that they can achieve their close-to-optimal solution. Training and testing are performed under the very same conditions: a seven-fold cross validation scenario using predefined but random groups of the 259 high-grade glioma records of the BraTS 2019 training dataset. Thorough numerical evaluation suites revealed the superiority of the U-net based solution with respect to a great majority of the statistical accuracy benchmarks. The most relevant quality indicator, namely the average Dice score, is approximately 2% higher for the U-net when segmenting edema, enhancing core or whole tumor, while there is no relevant difference between the two methods in the tumor core segmentation problem.

articleTitle: Innovation and Competitiveness: Theoretical Framework for Interactions
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: In the dynamic changes of the global economy, innovation plays a key role in maintaining and increasing competitiveness. The aim of our study is to explore the theoretical framework of the interactions between innovation and competitiveness, with a particular focus on the specificities of different industries and business environments. The research will examine the impact of innovation strategies on firms' market position and the role of product and process innovations in enhancing competitiveness through a literature review and empirical analysis. Our results show that successful innovation activities do not only involve technological improvements, but also the transformation of organisational cultures and processes. In developing the theoretical framework, we discuss an integrated approach to innovation systems that facilitates sustainable competitiveness enhancement in the corporate sector. This paper contributes to a deeper understanding of the theory of competitiveness and innovation and provides practical recommendations for firms.

articleTitle: NeuralODE-based Parameter Identification of the Three Chamber Model of the Circulatory System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: In cases of Acute Circulatory Failure, fluid therapy is a commonly used intervention to stabilize heart function. However, the effectiveness of fluid therapy is not directly predictable, and the therapy can also be harmful. Physiological models can be used to predict fluid responsiveness - describing the effectiveness of fluid therapy for the patient - but require solving complex parameter identification problems. The current study aims to develop a Physics Informed Neural Network, specifically a NeuralODE-based parameter identification method for the Three Chamber cardiovascular model, which has the potential to be used to define a novel perfusion marker. The method is developed and validated on a clinical data set collected in model animal experiments.

articleTitle: Navigating the AI Revolution: Employee Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the corporate landscape, automating tasks, augmenting decision-making, and reshaping industries. While AI offers immense potential, its impact on employees is a critical concern. This study examines the intricate relationship between AI adoption and employee attitudes, focusing on trust, job security, work-life balance, well-being, and res killing. By analyzing corporate employee sentiment through a quantitative methodology, this study aims to provide valuable insights for organizations navigating the AI revolution. The findings reveal that trust in AI's capabilities is a critical factor influencing employee confidence and acceptance of AI-driven decision-making. Additionally, while res killing initiatives are essential for preparing employees for the AI-driven future, they may not directly address concerns about job security. By prioritizing employee well-being and addressing anxieties related to future shock, organizations can harness the power of AI to create a more positive and productive workplace.

articleTitle: From Concepts to Applications: A Comprehensive Overview of ROS
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: This paper explores the Robot Operating System (ROS), a foundational open-source middleware designed to facilitate robotics development by integrating hardware and software. It provides essential tools and algorithms enabling efficient programming of complex robotic systems. This work delves into the core components of ROS, including its computational graph model, parameter servers, and messaging systems, while highlighting tools that enhance system capabilities. Additionally, the paper reviews navigation algorithms, from traditional ones to advanced path-planning techniques, emphasizing their applications in autonomous mobile robotics. Comparisons of robotics software platforms illustrate the diversity and adaptability required to meet the demands of modern robotics. In the end, this paper emphasizes its critical role in advancing academic research and industrial applications.

articleTitle: From Innovation to Implementation: Leveraging AI-Driven Automation in Smart Urban Railway Operations
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: As public transport continues to evolve, technological innovations, in particular the application of artificial intelligence (AI), open up new opportunities to improve operational efficiency, which can contribute to smart urban mobility solutions, more complex analysis and development of traffic management tools. With decades of experience from operating companies, best practices, data science and machine learning (ML), it would be possible to automate some operational tasks and introduce intelligent operations. This paper attempts to outline the technological possibilities such as computer vision, anomaly detection, natural language processing (NLP) and knowledge mining, while, at the same time, explores the challenges in specific areas of operations, such as automation of sensor data processing from vehicles, or new approaches to modern work.

articleTitle: Interpretation and Meaning of Agility in Relation to Individual Identification with it
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Understanding and applying agility is key in the 21st century, as it contributes significantly to the success of companies and individuals in a rapidly changing business environment. Agility enables organisations to respond quickly to market changes and new challenges. In the market economy of the 21st century, companies are constantly faced with new challenges and only those that can adapt quickly can succeed. Agile companies can gain a competitive advantage by reacting faster to market developments. They create value for consumers more efficiently and are characterised by continuous innovation and improvement. Agility is not only a methodological issue, but also an important element in the development of organisational culture and human resources. An agile approach fosters collaboration and teamwork, increases employee engagement and motivation, and improves leadership skills and decision-making processes. It is important to note that implementing and maintaining agility can be challenging. Successful agile transformation requires, first and foremost, leadership commitment and support, which in many cases goes hand in hand with changes to organisational structures and processes. Yet the most important factor in the process is the people themselves. To successfully adapt agile values to the organisation, it is also necessary to train and develop employees. Our research investigated the meaning and meaning of agility as a function of individual identification based on the results of primary research among Arab and Hungarian youth. The questionnaire survey in the two cultures aimed to explore the cultural and contextual differences and identities of the concept of agility. The survey asked participants about their visions of agility, asking them to tell us what agility means to them. The results revealed that although the basic principles of agility - flexibility, adaptability and openness to innovation - are present in both countries, there were significant differences in the detailed understanding of the concept and its practical application.

articleTitle: Fuel Composition's Impact on Small Jet Engine Mathematical Modelling
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to highlight the impact of applying alternative fuels on the mathematical models of jet engines. The analysis focuses on the class of small jet engines, while the presented findings can be generalized to other classes of aircraft engines. The results are illustrated in the characteristics of jet engine components and define the influence of alternative fuels on them. To this end, the paper provides an introductory overview of methods for developing mathematical models while considering the application of sustainable aviation fuels as well as insights to measurement of emission characteristics of turbojet engines.

articleTitle: Information Entropy-Driven Sequential Fuzzy Indexed Search Trees for Human Activity Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Real-time activity recognition is an important field of machine learning, which can provide useful information about the people inhabiting the observed space. In this paper, a novel system is proposed that uses a so-called Information Entropy-driven Sequential Fuzzy Indexed Search Trees classifier that realizes fast activity recognition, using pose information from the output of a real-time multi-person keypoint detection framework that detects human bodies in image frames and outputs a set of keypoints. The proposed system implements a flexible expert knowledge-based classification in the form of indexing tables and binary search trees, to significantly reduce the search area of the problem space that needs to be regarded during the recognition phase, and thus, significantly lowering the required operation time. The performance of the method is evaluated on five datasets and compared to the performance of two state-of-the-art classifiers.

articleTitle: Expert-Recommendation System for Assessing and Improving Airmen's Language Skills Following International Standards
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 12th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: A study of developing an expert-recommended system for assessing and improving the language abilities of individuals for aviation activities according to the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standards in the context of ensuring the safety and efficiency of aviation activities has been conducted. The expert-recommended system consists of three stages of assessment based on the following approaches: a model for the formal evaluation of airmen's language abilities according to ICAO standards, a fuzzy expert model for the level of language abilities evaluation, an aggregated model for deriving recommendations for improving the language abilities of individuals for aviation activities according to international standards. The study is based on the modern mathematical theory of fuzzy logic and fuzzy sets, expert assessment, and intellectual analysis of knowledge. The system makes it possible to obtain an evaluation of the language abilities of individuals according to ICAO standards, as well as the linguistic level of the abilities of individuals for aviation activities and recommendations for optimal ways to improve language abilities. The expert-recommendation system was verified on 1116 accurate data of 93 applicants from the Language Assessment Body 009 certified by the Transport Authority of the Slovak Republic at the Faculty of Aeronautics of the Technical University of Košice (FA TUKE). The proposed system is usable in all similarly certified bodies for these purposes.
